title: The fall of Jerusalem and the new call
source_text: Καὶ Χριστιανοὶ δὲ κατὰ τὸν Κέλσον προστιθέντες τινὰς λόγους τοῖς ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων λεγομένοις φασὶ διὰ τὰς τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἁμαρτίας ἤδη πεπέμφθαι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ὅτι Ἰουδαῖοι κολάσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ χολὴν ποτίσαντες ἐπὶ σφᾶς αὐτοὺς ἐκ θεοῦ χόλον ἐπεσπάσαντο. ἐλεγχέτω δὴ τὸ λεγόμενον ὡς ψεῦδος ὁ βουλόμενος, εἰ μὴ ἀνάστατον τὸ πάντων Ἰουδαίων ἔθνος γεγένηται οὐδὲ μετὰ γενεὰν ὅλην μίαν τοῦ ταῦτα πεπονθέναι ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν τὸν Ἰησοῦν· τεσσαράκοντα γὰρ ἔτη καὶ δύο οἶμαι ἀφ᾿ οὗ ἐσταύρωσαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν γεγονέναι ἐπὶ τὴν Ἱεροσολύμων καθαίρεσιν. καὶ οὐδέ ποτε γὲ ἱστόρηται, ἐξ οὗ Ἰουδαῖοί εἰσι, τοσοῦτον αὐτοὺς χρόνον ἐκβεβλῆσθαι τῆς σεμνῆς ἁγιστείας καὶ λατρείας, κρατηθέντας ὑπὸ δυνατωτέρων· ἀλλ᾿ εἰ καί ποτε ἔδοξαν δι᾿ ἁμαρτίας καταλείπεσθαι. οὐδὲν ἧττον ἐπεσκοπήθησαν καὶ ἐπανελθόντες τὰ ἴδια ἀπειλήφασιν, ἀκωλύτως ποιοῦντες τὰ νενομισμένα. ἓν οὖν τῶν παριστάντων θεῖόν τι καὶ ἱερὸν χρῆμα γεγονέναι τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐστι καὶ τὸ Ἰουδαίοις ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ τοσαῦτα καὶ τοιαῦτα πολλῷ ἤδη συμβεβηκέναι χρόνῳ. θαῤῥοῦντες δ᾿ ἐροῦμεν ὅτι οὐδ᾿ ἀποκατασταθήσονται. ἄγος γὰρ ἔπραξαν τὸ πάντων ἀνοσιώτατον. τῷ σωτῆρι τοῦ γένους τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπιβουλεύσαντες ἐν τῇ πόλει, ἔνθα τὰ νενομισμένα σύμβολα μεγάλων μυστηρίων ἐποίουν τῷ θεῷ. ἐχρῆν οὖν ἐκείνην τὴν πόλιν, ὅπου ταῦτα πέπονθεν Ἰησοῦς, ἄρδην ἀπολωλέναι καὶ τὸ Ἰουδαίων ἔθνος ἀνάστατον γεγονέναι καὶ ἐπ᾿ ἄλλους τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς μακαριότητα κλῆσιν μεταβεβηκέναι, τοὺς Χριστιανοὺς λέγω, ἐφ᾿ οὓς ἐλήλυθεν ἡ περὶ τῆς εἰλικρινοῦς καὶ καθαρᾶς θεοσεβείας διδασκαλία, παραλαβόντας νόμους καινοὺς καὶ ἁρμόζοντας τῇ πανταχοῦ καθεστώσῃ πολιτείᾳ· ἐπεὶ μὴ οἱ πρότερον δοθέντες ὡς ἑνὶ ἔθνει, ὑπὸ οἰκείων καὶ ὁμοήθων βασιλευομένῳ, οἷοί τε ἦσαν πάντες νῦν ἐπιτελεῖσθαι.
pass_a_gloss: And Christians too, according to (κατά) Celsus, adding (προστίθημι) certain words to the things said by Jews, say that because of the sins (ἁμαρτίαι) of the Jews the Son of God has already been sent (πέμπω), and that Jews, having punished (κολάζω) Jesus and having given him gall (χολή) to drink (ποτίζω), drew upon (ἐπισπάω) themselves wrath (χόλος) from God. Let the one who wishes refute (ἐλέγχω) the thing said as a lie (ψεῦδος), if the nation (ἔθνος) of all the Jews has not become overthrown/uprooted (ἀνάστατος) not even after one whole generation (γενεά) from Jesus having suffered (πάσχω) these things by them; for forty and two years, I think, came to be from when they crucified (σταυρόω) Jesus to the destruction (καθαίρεσις) of Jerusalem. And never has it been recorded (ἱστορέω), since (ἐξ οὗ) Jews exist, that they were thrown out (ἐκβάλλω) for so long a time from the venerable (σεμνός) ritual (ἁγιστεία) and worship (λατρεία), overpowered (κρατέω) by the more powerful (δυνατώτεροι); but even if at some time they seemed (δοκέω) to be left behind/abandoned (καταλείπω) through sins, none the less (οὐδὲν ἧττον) they were visited (ἐπισκοπέω, passive) and, having returned (ἐπανέρχομαι), took back (ἀπολαμβάνω) their own, doing unhindered (ἀκωλύτως) the customary things (τὰ νενομισμένα). One, then, of the things presenting (παρίστημι) Jesus to have been a divine and holy thing (θεῖον καὶ ἱερὸν χρῆμα) is also that so many and such things have befallen (συμβαίνω) Jews on account of him (ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ) for much time already. Being confident (θαρρέω) we shall say that they will not even be restored (ἀποκαθίστημι). For they did (πράσσω) a pollution/crime (ἄγος) the most unholy (ἀνοσιώτατον) of all, having plotted against (ἐπιβουλεύω) the Saviour (σωτήρ) of the race of men, in the city where they used to perform (ποιέω) to God the customary symbols (σύμβολα) of great mysteries (μυστήρια). It was needful (ἐχρῆν) therefore that that city, where Jesus suffered these things, be utterly (ἄρδην) destroyed (ἀπόλλυμι), and the nation of the Jews become overthrown, and the call (κλῆσις) of God to blessedness (μακαριότης) pass over (μεταβαίνω) to others, the Christians I mean, upon whom has come the teaching (διδασκαλία) about sincere (εἰλικρινής) and pure (καθαρά) piety toward God (θεοσέβεια), having received (παραλαμβάνω) new laws (νόμοι καινοί) and fitting (ἁρμόζω) the constitution/way of life (πολιτεία) established (καθίστημι) everywhere (πανταχοῦ); since those given earlier, as to one nation ruled as by a king by its own and like-customed people, were not all able now to be fulfilled.
pass_b_english: According to Celsus, the Christians add some further points to what the Jews say, and claim that the Son of God has already been sent because of the sins of the Jews, and that the Jews, by punishing Jesus and giving him gall to drink (Matthew 27:34), drew down wrath from God upon themselves.

Let anyone who wishes prove this statement false, if the whole Jewish nation was not overthrown before even one full generation had passed since Jesus suffered these things at their hands. For it was, I think, forty-two years from the time they crucified Jesus to the destruction of Jerusalem. And never, since there have been Jews, has it been recorded that they were shut out for so long a time from their venerable rites and worship, overpowered by those stronger than they. But even if at times they seemed to be abandoned because of their sins, they were none the less visited, and they returned and recovered what was their own, performing their customary rites without hindrance. So one of the facts that show Jesus to have been something divine and holy is this: that on his account so many and such great calamities have now befallen the Jews for a long time.

We shall say with confidence that they will not even be restored. For they committed the most unholy crime of all, when they plotted against the Saviour of the human race in the very city where they used to perform for God the customary rites that were symbols of great mysteries. It was necessary, then, that the city where Jesus suffered these things should be utterly destroyed, that the Jewish nation should be overthrown, and that God’s call to blessedness should pass to others, I mean the Christians. To them has come the teaching of sincere and pure devotion to God, and they have received new laws suited to the order of life established everywhere, since the laws given earlier, as to one nation ruled by kings of its own race and customs, could not all be carried out now.

Celsus's report of the Christians is indirect in the Greek and is kept as indirect speech. 'τινὰς λόγους' rendered 'some further points'. 'χολὴν ποτίσαντες ... χόλον ἐπεσπάσαντο' is a pun (gall / wrath) that English cannot carry; rendered plainly as 'gall' and 'wrath', with no word added to imitate it. The gall refers to Matthew 27:34 (wine mixed with gall), itself echoing Psalm 69:21 (LXX 68:22); only Matthew is cited inline. 'οὐδὲ μετὰ γενεὰν ὅλην μίαν' rendered 'before even one full generation had passed'; it may recall Matthew 23:36 or 24:34 ('this generation'), but this is uncertain and not cited. Origen's 'forty-two years, I think' is his own reckoning from the crucifixion to the fall of Jerusalem in AD 70. ἐπεσκοπήθησαν is passive with no named agent; rendered 'they were visited' (the biblical sense of God's visiting), without supplying 'by God' or 'again'. 'θεῖόν τι καὶ ἱερὸν χρῆμα' rendered 'something divine and holy'. 'τοσαῦτα καὶ τοιαῦτα' rendered 'so many and such great calamities'; the noun is supplied from context (the overthrow and exile just described). 'σύμβολα' rendered 'rites that were symbols', since the symbols were acts performed (ἐποίουν). 'ἄρδην ἀπολωλέναι' may recall Luke 19:43–44 and 'the call ... should pass to others' may recall Matthew 21:43; both uncertain, not cited. θεοσέβεια rendered 'devotion to God'. 'τῇ πανταχοῦ καθεστώσῃ πολιτείᾳ' rendered 'the order of life established everywhere'. βασιλευομένῳ rendered 'ruled by kings'. This passage states Origen's view of the Jewish people after the crucifixion; it is translated as written, without softening or comment in the reading text.
